requirements.statement: The stable release conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA for the declared supported profiles.
Every structural pointer operation has an equivalent keyboard and programmatic command.
Tabs and splitters implement the applicable WAI-ARIA interaction patterns.
Announcements describe final semantic outcomes and are localizable, replaceable, and rate-controlled.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Screen-reader task recordings and message catalog audit.

requirements.statement: Workspace controls remain operable at 400% zoom and in forced-colors mode.
Reduced motion removes non-essential spatial movement and does not merely shorten every duration.
Color, motion, hover, or precision dragging is the sole means of communicating state or invoking a structural action.
Voice-control-friendly accessible names remain stable and specific across panels and actions.
All hard release gates and all MUST requirements in the normative register pass for every stable supported profile.
Any exception changes the published support claim or releases under an experimental label.
The implementation demonstrates useful superiority through robust outcomes, not feature count or visual polish alone.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Quality scorecard and comparative workload study.

requirements.statement: Panel parameters and checkpoints are inferred statically and validated at trust boundaries.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Type tests and runtime schema tests.

requirements.statement: Commands, queries, subscriptions, lifecycle, and operational effects are separate public concepts.
Consumers mutate exposed entity objects or reconstruct truth from events alone.
Expected asynchronous failures return typed result values with stable codes and remediation.
Selectors avoid unrelated recomputation and framework rerender.
First useful workspace setup completes in under ten minutes for an unfamiliar engineer.
Custom panel type setup completes in under fifteen minutes without reading internal source.
Advanced Effect and protocol APIs are available without forcing them onto ordinary consumers.
The headless model and kernel have no DOM, framework, Effect-runtime, XState, or animation dependency.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Package graph and Node.js execution tests.

requirements.statement: XState actors exist only for active bounded protocols and are disposed when their owning scope closes.
Effect wraps fallible operations without imposing fiber scheduling on ordinary synchronous kernel reads and commits.
Motion drivers implement a stable internal port and do not appear in persisted data.
The production runtime pins tested library versions and exposes compatibility through adapters rather than broad re-export.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Lockfile, package manifest, and API-surface audit.

requirements.statement: Personal layout is the default collaboration mode unless the product explicitly enables shared layout.
Durable collaboration replicates semantic transactions, not pointer frames or raw DOM events.
Every protocol packet is versioned, schema-validated, session-bound, epoch-bound, and transaction-identified.
At most one authoritative owner exists for each panel instance.
Coordinator loss, duplicate delivery, reordering, and stale epochs have defined recovery behavior.
Presence and preview traffic uses a separate lossy channel from durable transactions.
Every panel, group, node, surface, transaction, and motion target has a stable explicit identifier.
A DOM node, framework instance, array position, or window handle serves as persistent identity.
Derived geometry and runtime resources are excluded from canonical serialization except documented restore hints.
Application panel state and workspace layout state have separate codecs, versions, and failure handling.
Visual tombstones are inert, aria-hidden, pointer-inactive, and hard-bounded in lifetime.
Every structural operation exposes a human-readable command label and deterministic outcome.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Command registry audit and usability tasks.

requirements.statement: The visible drop preview is produced from the same solver and policy result used by commit.
Every completed direct-manipulation gesture creates at most one workspace-history entry.
A failed or blocked external capability keeps content in a safe in-page location.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Popup, permission, and surface failure tests.

requirements.statement: A new consumer can render a typed panel workspace in under ten minutes using stable public APIs.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Timed DX study with unfamiliar engineers.

requirements.statement: Extensions use documented registries, ports, policies, and contribution values rather than private internals.
Plugin manifests, protocol messages, persisted namespaces, and panel data are versioned and schema-validated.
Plugin ordering and conflicts are deterministic and diagnosable.
A plugin mutates canonical state or attaches unscoped global listeners through a supported API.
Unavailable or failed plugins do not erase persisted panels or placements.
Third-party adapters can run the public conformance suite and publish certification metadata.
Selection, activation, DOM focus, and frontmost-surface state remain distinct in model and API.
Clicking an interactive descendant does not lose its natural focus merely to activate a panel.
Every close, move, transfer, restore, and projection change has deterministic focus recovery.
Focus is correct immediately after semantic commit and does not wait for animation.
Ordinary floating panels use modal semantics or focus trapping.
Panel renderers may provide stable restoration tokens for meaningful descendants across remount.
Every supported framework adapter passes the same semantic and lifecycle contract suite.
Geometry frames and pointer movement do not trigger workspace-wide framework reconciliation.
Framework development modes do not duplicate ownership or leak resources.
SSR-safe imports and deterministic hydration are documented for supported configurations.
Cross-document context preservation is explicit and capability-negotiated.
Adapter-specific APIs remain idiomatic without changing core semantics.
Each implementation phase has objective exit evidence and does not rely on demo appearance.
Public API, persisted schema, surface protocol, and experimental capabilities have explicit versioning policies.
A failed conformance gate cannot be waived for a stable release without changing the support claim.
Core ownership, invariant, transaction, lifecycle, and protocol changes require architecture decision records.
Deprecations provide diagnostics and mechanical migration support where feasible.
Third-party adapters and plugins can publish machine-readable compatibility and conformance metadata.
All user-visible library text is localizable and avoids English-specific concatenation.
Logical axes, RTL, and supported writing modes are reflected in layout, movement, resizing, and announcements.
Platform shortcut names and numeric values are formatted through locale-aware services.
Direct pointer manipulation writes visual state at most once per surface animation frame.
Raw pointer coordinates do not enter canonical state, persistence, or transaction history.
Escape, pointer cancellation, capture loss, and scope disposal leave no residual interaction state.
Every structural pointer action has keyboard, menu or command-palette, and programmatic equivalents.
Drop previews are policy-valid, solver-exact, labeled, and reversible.
Pointer resize is direct; content resize notifications may be live, throttled, deferred, or adaptive by declared policy.
Target hysteresis prevents oscillation without creating a magnetic offset that impairs precision.
Docked layout uses n-ary splits and canonical flattening of adjacent same-axis nodes.
All semantic axes and edges are logical and writing-mode aware.
Resolved child pixels plus splitters exactly equal available pixels after rounding.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Property tests across fractional sizes and DPRs.

requirements.statement: Infeasible constraints produce an explicit policy outcome and diagnostic, never negative or inaccessible geometry.
The speculative preview and committed result use the same constraint implementation.
A local topology or constraint change invalidates only affected branches and surface indexes.
Stable integer or fixed-point weights prevent cumulative resize drift.
The lifecycle state machine and callback ordering are public compatibility contracts.
Every successful mount has exactly one eventual finalization; duplicate disposal is harmless at the boundary.
Hidden content is inert and excluded from accessibility traversal while preserving declared lifecycle state.
Cross-document transfer has an explicit checkpoint/remount or mirror contract.
Failed transfer retains or recovers the panel in a safe authoritative surface.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Failure injection after every protocol step.

requirements.statement: Lifecycle callbacks carry cancellation and revision context and cannot mutate canonical state directly.
Visibility reasons allow applications to pause expensive work without conflating selection and document visibility.
The canonical state satisfies all published invariants after every committed transaction.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Invariant checker in development, test, and import paths.

requirements.statement: Canonicalization is deterministic and idempotent.
Each relationship has exactly one authoritative representation in canonical state.
The optimized kernel is differentially tested against a reference implementation after every generated command.
NaN, infinity, negative dimensions, duplicate ownership, or cycles are accepted into a committed state.
Unchanged public entity values preserve referential identity across revisions.
Direct drag and pointer resize have no delayed smoothing between input and controlled object.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: High-speed pointer trace and visual-latency measurement.

requirements.statement: Semantic commit, focus, accessibility state, and lifecycle do not wait for motion completion.
Every running animation belongs to a disposable Scope with finish, cancel, skip, and cleanup behavior.
A re-grab samples current visual geometry and begins without a jump exceeding one CSS pixel.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Interruption tests at sampled progress points.

requirements.statement: Closing content is semantically removed before an inert visual tombstone exits.
The library ships a repeating strobe, full-panel luminance flash, or motion-only status indicator.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Preset audit and automated flash analysis.

requirements.statement: View Transitions are optional progressive enhancement; skip or failure cannot prevent state change.
Cross-window transfer uses coordinated handoff rather than a claimed continuous cross-screen animation.
Layout, gesture, presence, clip, and emphasis channels cannot overwrite one another’s owned properties.
The planner degrades decoration before spatial continuity and never degrades direct input tracking.
The inspector can correlate a committed transaction across model, geometry, renderer, lifecycle, motion, persistence, and surface effects.
Diagnostic instrumentation is observational and cannot change command ordering or correctness.
Reproduction exports are deterministic, bounded, versioned, and redacted by default.
Expected errors and invariant defects are distinguishable in diagnostics and telemetry.
Property-based failures shrink to a minimal command and event sequence suitable for issue attachment.
Usage telemetry is disabled by default in the library.
Persistence separates kernel, application-layout, protocol, and panel-type versions.
Every previously supported schema has a tested migration or explicit non-destructive recovery path.
Snapshot and journal updates are atomic within the storage adapter’s transaction model.
Panel checkpoint data is durable before a canonical snapshot references it.
A missing panel type is represented by a recoverable placeholder rather than silently deleted.
Workspace undo is separate from application content undo and has explicit command scope.
Restoring external-window intent never requires automatic popup creation and never loses the panel.
Canonical serialization has stable ordering suitable for hashing and semantic diffing.
The package graph is acyclic and enforced in continuous integration.
Headless packages import without evaluating browser globals.
Optional platform and framework packages are not pulled through the default headless entry point.
Each package publishes a documented public entry-point map and compatibility policy.
The model and reference kernel have zero runtime dependencies.
Pointer movement and layout animation do not enter framework-wide render loops.
Performance results are reproducible from published workloads and machine-readable manifests.
The optimized implementation preserves reference-kernel semantics under differential testing.
No interaction, telemetry, persistence, or collaboration queue is unbounded.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Queue policy audit and stress tests.

requirements.statement: Lifecycle torture returns library-owned listeners, observers, actors, fibers, scopes, hosts, and animations to baseline tolerance.
Work scales with affected entities rather than total workspace size for ordinary local operations.
Motion performance is verified at both 60 Hz and 120 Hz.
Quality is assessed across all published supported profiles, not a selected favorable benchmark.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Automated scorecard with profile completeness check.

requirements.statement: Any failed hard gate sets the release-quality score to zero.
Benchmark results include hardware, browser, version, workload, sample count, and confidence interval.
Known limitations and unsupported configurations are published with every stable release.
The robust overall quality score is at least 0.90 and no dimension is below 0.80.
Same-document movement in stable-host mode preserves the panel content host and does not remount content.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mount counter tests with editor, map, iframe, and form fixtures.

requirements.statement: Geometry-frame updates bypass framework-wide rendering and update only affected DOM projection.
Every browser-facing operation uses the relevant surface document and window.
Overlay, shield, listener, observer, and host resources are finalized with their owning surface or interaction Scope.
Semantic chrome remains accessible even when content uses a stable flattened host plane.
A panel or group renderer failure is isolated and replaced by a recoverable error surface.
Every principal architectural risk has a named mitigation, test, owner, and decision trigger.
A limited use of a rejected alternative is documented at the boundary and cannot become canonical authority.
Complexity is justified by supported profile evidence rather than generalized abstraction ambition.
The project periodically removes extension points or modes that cannot be conformed or maintained.
Responsive adaptation is a reversible projection and does not mutate canonical layout implicitly.
Touch use does not depend on hover or precision pointing and respects scrolling and safe areas.
Every public capability is classified as stable, experimental, deprecated, or unsupported.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Generated API inventory and release manifest.

requirements.statement: Supported claims identify browser, framework, input, accessibility, and workload profiles.
The core promises unrestricted native-window behavior that the web platform cannot guarantee.
Application-owned panel state has an explicit codec, version, and migration boundary.
Every trust boundary validates a bounded schema and rejects malformed, excessive, NaN, infinite, or prototype-polluting input.
Cross-surface messages are authenticated to the workspace session and validated against epoch and revision.
The stable build is compatible with strict CSP and Trusted Types without eval or unsafe HTML requirements.
Telemetry and diagnostic exports redact panel titles, parameters, checkpoints, and application data by default.
Permission denial preserves normal functionality and content safety.
An invariant defect freezes structural mutation at the last valid snapshot and produces a redacted reproduction.
Stable releases publish provenance, dependency inventory, security policy, and vulnerability response expectations.
Runtime dependencies and privileged post-install behavior are minimized.
Every surface exposes explicit capabilities; commands and UI use capability intersection.
A browser-window destination is prepared and acknowledged before semantic ownership transfer.
Unexpected surface loss produces deterministic recovery without panel loss.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Close, crash, refresh, and coordinator-failure tests.

requirements.statement: Surface-specific DOM, style, locale, direction, and security context are explicit.
Restored geometry is clamped to available viewport and monitor configuration with a minimum visible region.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Monitor removal, zoom, and DPR tests.

requirements.statement: Multi-screen permission is required for normal single-screen functionality.
Picture-in-Picture is treated as a restricted optional surface and has an in-page fallback.
The semantic kernel is the sole authority for committed workspace state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Dependency graph review and mutation-path tests.

requirements.statement: The system separates semantic, protocol, spatial, motion, and operational concerns through typed contracts.
A successful semantic command remains correct when every optional animation is disabled or skipped.
No supported failure mode silently loses a panel or its recoverable descriptor.
The ordinary integration surface hides Effect and XState unless an application opts into advanced APIs.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: DX task study and public API review.

requirements.statement: The library imposes no global CSS reset, typography, icon set, or unscoped z-index policy.
Themes support forced colors, focus visibility, reduced motion, large text, and touch targets.
The kernel passes exhaustive bounded exploration and at least ten million generated semantic operations before stable release.
Reference and optimized kernels agree after every generated command.
Every documented protocol transition, interruption, timeout, and recovery path is tested with deterministic time.
Multi-window ownership invariants are model-checked or equivalently exhaustively verified under message reordering and crash injection.
Every supported framework and browser profile passes the same applicable conformance suite.
Performance CI detects statistically meaningful regressions and preserves raw traces.
Stable release requires manual accessibility evidence, not automated scanning alone.
Motion-off runs produce equivalent canonical state and focus outcomes.
Failure-injection tests establish the final authoritative location or placeholder for every panel.
All semantic mutation passes through the command transaction path.
Subscribers never observe partially reduced or partially canonicalized state.
Commands dispatched during commit notification are queued for a later transaction.
Prepared external resources are rolled back when revalidation or commit fails.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Failure injection at every prepare step.

requirements.statement: Post-commit effects carry transaction ID and revision and are safe under duplicate delivery where retryable.
Policy denial includes a stable code and user-actionable explanation.
The final commit revalidates policies and base revision after any asynchronous preparation.
A completed gesture is represented by one semantic command or one explicit atomic batch.
